highlights.summary: After it was announced that Sony was dropping Hideo Kojima's Physint, and that instead the Metal Gear Solid creator's latest title would be coming to Xbox, there were a flurry of rumors about the falling out.
body: It released a statement saying ‘the studio is in a healthy, profitable state.’

I know there’s a lot of news in the game industry that many studios are closing down, many titles are canceled, and I understand the situation in the industry as a whole. But I thought Physint was okay. That Physint was safe. So I was surprised … If we lose one contract, I thought I might have to cut all the people working on Physint, right? Or our studio could end up collapsing because we’ll run out of cashflow.

The company has now taken to social media to state that, despite reports about disappointing sales of Death Stranding and its sequel, and the loss of funding from Sony, it is “in a healthy, profitable state.” And that, moreover, its “relationship with PlayStation remains strong.”

highlights.title: ScrollEd wants to turn textbooks into TikTok
highlights.summary: ScrollEd turns textbooks into a scrollable, Instagram-like feed with video, audio, and quizzes. The Palo Alto startup, founded by student co-founders (and spouses) Utsav Gupta and Rebecca Neff, pitches at TechCrunch Disrupt.
body: Society has spent a lot of time bemoaning our digitally addled minds and goldfish-like attention spans, pointing the finger of blame at doomscrolling as the reason we can’t just sit down and read a book or study for exams. But what if the solution isn’t to stop scrolling, but to rethink what we’re scrolling through?

That’s the bet startup ScrollEd is making. The Palo Alto-based startup is pitching in the TechCrunch Disrupt Startup Battlefield 200 competition with the novel idea that if students won’t open a textbook, the textbook should open itself up to them — as a scroll.

ScrollEd has built an app that allows the user to turn any text file — including dry PDFs or text books — into a feed that feels a lot like Instagram Reels or TikTok. As you scroll, the content shows up as AI-generated video, audio, text, or even interactive quizzes. Swiping up surfaces a new topic, while swiping sideways lets you go deeper into the one you’re on, with a quiz waiting for you at the end.

highlights.summary: Matheus Cunha's deflected 89th-minute strike grabbed Manchester United a 1-1 draw at Fulham to take the edge off what appeared to be turning into a full-blown crisis for Michael Carrick's side going into the international break.
body: A horror-show own goal from Lisandro Martinez with 23 minutes to play, piled the pressure on United to snatch something from this match, following the midweek Carabao Cup collapse at home to Brighton and Manchester derby defeat last weekend.

A wicked flick off David Affengruber got them out of jail. But United are still in the bottom half of the Premier League after five games, 10 points adrift of table-topping neighbours City and looking miles off the level required to challenge the country's best sides this season. This is their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign.
Manchester United have won just five points from five league games this season – their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign (also 5 in 2014-15).

"A real mess" was how Sky Sports' Gary Neville described the own goal. Cunha was levered off the ball by Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey, whose stinging shot was parried by Senne Lammens. The 'keeper then saw Martinez stick out a boot and divert the ball back past him. Lammens' clumsy attempt to cut it out summed up United's chaotic defending.

highlights.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Hits Harder Than Ever
highlights.summary: There are certain lines of dialogue that become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context because the words have long since transcended their…
body: Star Trek: The Original Series has plenty of those. Spock’s wish that everyone to “live long and prosper” is arguably the franchise's signature phrase. He also turned the simple word “fascinating” into a catchphrase simply by raising one eyebrow before saying it. Dr. McCoy (DeForest Kelley) spent three seasons reminding everyone, “I'm a doctor, not a…” and, at least in our collective memory declaring, “He's dead, Jim” while standing over the latest redshirt who wandered a little too far from the landing party.

On the surface, it doesn't seem like an obvious choice. It's not printed on T-shirts nearly as often as “live long and prosper.” It isn't endlessly quoted by people who have never watched an episode of Star Trek. And unlike “beam me up, Scotty,” it never became part of the broader pop culture vocabulary. But that's exactly why it's the best quote. It doesn't just capture Kirk. It captures the entire philosophy of Star Trek.

highlights.title: Christopher Kane and Mulberry make swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week
highlights.summary: Appointment of Kane as creative director signals the return of serious style ambition for former It-bag brand. With spicy leather mini-dresses and shoes with miniature axes for heels, two beloved British names made a swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week.
body: Fifteen years ago, Christopher Kane and Mulberry were two of the biggest shows on the line-up. Kane was the brilliant young designer who could find fashion in the most unlikely places: rubberised lace minis were inspired by “Princess Margaret on acid”; while illustrations from the 1972 classic The Joy of Sex appeared on slinky slip dresses. Mulberry was London’s home-grown It-bag brand: anyone who was anyone had a Bayswater or an Alexa.

On paper, it is an unlikely match. Mulberry is rooted in its Somerset factories and makes understated practical bags; Kane has a flair for bad-girl party dresses learned on the streets of Glasgow where he grew up.

Where they meet is leather. There were leather sheath dresses and elegantly spare leather car coats, as well as heeled loafers featuring Mulberry’s signature postman’s lock. Kane builds each collection around one visual motif – Frankenstein, gorillas, the reproductive organs of plants – and for this collection, took the castellated leather flaps of Mulberry’s Bayswater bags and turned them into notched hems and necklines. This was punchy, full-throttle fashion, accessorised with money-making bags and shoes.

In the rambling post, Trump said that data centers were “wealthy and prestigious” and claimed without evidence that they raised salaries, lowered taxes, and made for safer streets in the communities in which they were built. highlights.title: It’s Donald Trump Versus MAGA on Data Centers
highlights.summary: The president has doubled down on data centers and AI. His base is running in the opposite direction.
body: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at [email protected] or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.

Molly McCann Sanders has a lot in common with many of the other women who helped Donald Trump win a second term as president. A pro-life Catholic who lives in Texas, she has staunchly conservative opinions on immigration and a fierce hatred of eminent domain—the practice of the government taking private property for public use.

Sanders, the president of the Eagle Forum Education & Legal Defense Fund, which was started by Phyllis Schlafly, also describes herself as “a crunchy MAHA mom”—and says she’s been paying particular attention to data centers.
“I'm alarmed by the idea that these data centers can move in and pollute,” she tells me. “I'm not a data center expert. I'm not a tech expert. But I’m suspicious and wary, and want to move slowly.”

highlights.title: Palace secure valuable point at unbeaten Leeds
highlights.summary: Crystal Palace secured a useful point at in-form and unbeaten Leeds as Pierre Sage's side produced a much-improved defensive display to hold the hosts to a goalless draw at Elland Road.
body: The stalemate was enough to lift Sage's side one point clear of the relegation zone heading into the three-week international break.

Palace arrived having conceded 11 goals in their opening four Premier League games but, after a cagey first half, grew into the contest and were the more threatening side after the break. Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net only for it to be ruled out for offside.

Leeds, unbeaten coming into the game after an impressive 4-1 win over Newcastle, struggled to reproduce that attacking fluency. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who had scored in each of his previous five Premier League home games, was largely starved of service, eventually being denied by Walter Benitez after the break.

Palace had chances to snatch it late on, with Adam Wharton continuing to influence proceedings and Eddie Nketiah and Ismaila Sarr combining for an opening that Tarik Muharemovic brilliantly recovered to stop. Leeds threw on attacking reinforcements and switched shape, but could not find the breakthrough.

highlights.title: Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship, McIlroy falters despite late surge
highlights.summary: JJ Spaun outlasted a packed leaderboard of players on Sunday at the BMW PGA Championship, as the American capitalised on a stumble from Spain's Manuel Elvira to win his debut title at Wentworth.
body: An utterly thrilling final round of golf unfolded at Wentworth, with multiple players, including Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Elvira, racing to the finish line, but all struggled to pull away from the pack.
There was heartbreak for Elvira, who had the chance to leapfrog Spaun at the top of the leaderboard after tying the 2025 US Open champion with an eagle on the 17th hole.

With Spaun already in the clubhouse at 17 under, the Spaniard, who is ranked 294th in the Official World Golf Rankings, needed a birdie on the 18th to win his first-ever DP World Tour title, but he stumbled, finding a fairway bunker with his tee shot before sending his bunker shot well past the green.
He attempted to chip back on but agonisingly sent his shot into the bunker before ultimately confirming Spaun's two-stroke win with a double bogey.

highlights.title: Fire Emblem Is Officially Nintendo’s Strongest GOTY 2026 Contender
highlights.summary: I don't think I had "Fire Emblem gets a Game of the Year nomination at The Game Awards" on my bingo card for 2026 — or for any other year, for that matter. But I think it's a possibility. In fact, I think it's almost definitely going to happen. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is a contender.
body: That doesn't mean it's going to win. It increasingly looks like nothing will come even close to getting in Grand Theft Auto 6 's way. But it does mean that, in a weak field, Nintendo and developer Intelligent Systems have muscled their way to the front of the pack through sheer force of conviction.

Fire Emblem would once have been considered far too niche to attract Game of the Year attention from The Game Awards jury. It's an RPG, sure — one of the jurors' favored genres. But it's also a tactics RPG. It's basically a strategy game, and no strategy game has ever secured a GOTY nomination.

Things started to change for Intelligent Systems' series in the 2010s, though. First, there was Fire Emblem Awakening for the 3DS, which is still widely considered the best entry in the series. It attracted enough critical acclaim to start to break through with players who weren't particular fans of the genre. Gaming's cognoscenti took notice.

highlights.title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show
highlights.summary: Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus. Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister.
body: Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

Lee’s spring/summer 2027 show took place in the unusual setting of a north London school sports hall. Starmer wore a bright turquoise knitted midi dress with a high neckline, pleated detailing and short, sculptural sleeves, paired with white block-heeled shoes, with her hair worn in loose waves.

Rather than preparations for the show taking place backstage in the usual way, in Lee’s unique show, models were fitted and adjusted in full view of the audience, dancers rehearsed beside the catwalk, while a drone followed proceedings from the high ceiling of the gymnasium.

Starmer was photographed having her makeup done beside the catwalk, against a backdrop of a football net, with makeup and hair products spread out over a table in front of her. Ballerinas stretched beside the catwalk and synchronised swimming-inspired dancers performed in bright red costumes as part of the show, in the school in Chalk Farm.

highlights.summary: To paraphrase a former Manchester United manager, Michael Carrick knew that the storm would come. Everything went a little too perfectly for him in the second half of last season. There would be ill winds at some point. Which was what Carrick could feel before this visit to Fulham.
body: Relief was surely the main thing. Because after the derby defeat by Manchester City last Sunday and the midweek Carabao Cup exit against Brighton – both at Old Trafford – Carrick was starring at an unwanted hat-trick. All this on the back of other wobbles since the opening weekend when United lost at Hull.

It was a darkly comic own goal by Lisandro Martínez that raised Fulham’s hopes of a first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa. United have almost always won in this corner of south-west London in recent seasons. A crash against the team that started at the foot of the table was unthinkable.

Carrick and his team averted disaster when they caught a huge break with time almost up. There was little on for Matheus Cunha on the edge of the area, to the left of centre, and so he took on the shot for the near corner. The Fulham goalkeeper, Bernd Leno, looked to have it covered. Cue an almighty deflection off David Affengruber to send the ball spinning into the opposite corner.
points: To paraphrase a former Manchester United manager, Michael Carrick knew that the storm would come.
Everything went a little too perfectly for him in the second half of last season.
Which was what Carrick could feel before this visit to Fulham.
Because after the derby defeat by Manchester City last Sunday and the midweek Carabao Cup exit against Brighton – both at Old Trafford – Carrick was starring at an unwanted hat-trick.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
highlights.summary: Meta's Muse is apparently an effective AI assistant, but one that's a little creepy. Part of that is because of its new Mac app, which can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes. But for all its smarts, Muse doesn't actually know how to describe itself.
body: Muse probably can’t ‘see’ your notifications. But it also has no idea how it works.

The problem is that Aten says he didn’t give Muse access to his messages. When asked how it knew about the contents of his messages, Muse replied, “I saw the notification previews, not your message history. I haven’t been reading your texts.” Aten continued to push, asking how Muse was receiving message previews, it didn’t have a good answer. “Honest answer: I can’t give you the exact plumbing,” it said. “What I know is that the paired Mac app exposes notifications as one of its capabilities, and they arrive to me through the device sync.

In the conversation with his Muse in Jason’s screenshots, when Muse said it synced “device notifications”, it was confused about how to explain the feature and gave an incorrect explanation. That’s on us. We apologize for the incorrect response from Muse and we’re working to improve Muse’s understanding of its own internals so that it gives correct answers to questions about how it functions more consistently.

But for all its smarts, Muse doesn't actually know how to describe itself.

body: Nearly 20 years after founding CTAOP, the Oscar-winning actress reflected on its impact, which has helped close to 5 million people across South Africa – and on the overwhelming response to Christopher Nolan ’s The Odyssey and what it could signal for Hollywood going forward.

“It’s so rewarding to see that people do want to go to the theaters,” Theron told The Hollywood Reporter at the event. “They do want to go and see movies, and if we were ever questioning it, we shouldn’t anymore.”

Theron, who plays Calypso in Nolan’s epic, said the response has been particularly encouraging at a time when the industry remains uncertain about the future of moviegoing. “I do think my industry is really worried about where we are going and what’s happening,” she said. “I think we needed a little bit of this reminder that people do love to watch movies in the theater.”

highlights.title: Hungry for connection? This is what we lose when we stop eating together | Shadi Khan Saif
highlights.summary: Mealtimes offer a pause in the day for parents and children to sit together, listen to one another and trade stories. Making sense of it is a column about spirituality and how it can be used to navigate everyday life. When I was growing up in a Muslim household, food was rarely just food.
body: There was even a small ritual around something as ordinary as a piece of bread. If it fell on the ground anywhere in the house or was even seen on the ground outside, we would pick it up, clean it, kiss it respectfully and place it somewhere clean and safe. Food was not to be treated carelessly.
And sending a guest away without offering them a meal is unthinkable – almost a sin.
As a child, I didn’t think of any of this as “spirituality”. It was simply what you did. Eating alone felt like punishment. It still does.

Only later, after leaving Afghanistan and building a life in Australia, did I begin to understand what those ordinary habits carried with them: gratitude, hospitality and a sense that food was something to be celebrated – and shared.

highlights.title: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems
highlights.summary: Before recent high-profile hacks raised the specter of AI possibly " killing all humans," our energy systems were already disturbingly vulnerable to cyberattack - and the risk is growing. "We were always prey.
body: “We were always prey. We were just kind of surviving at the appetite of our predators,” Joshua Corman, executive in residence for public safety and resilience at the Institute for Security and Technology (IST), told me last year. At the time, I was preoccupied with a Department of Homeland Security warning that Iranian actors and sympathizers could target the US with cyberattacks.

Last week, I called Corman up to chat about recent incidents of rogue AI agents orchestrating their own complex cyberattacks. Even AI executives are talking about whether the technology they’re building could grow so out of control that it triggers an apocalypse. If there is now a 10 percent chance of artificial intelligence one day killing all humans, as some AI developers warn, surely there’s a chance it could knock our lights out in the meantime?
“Any sociopath that wants to [attack] is now more powerful than they used to be.”

body: The 21-year-old Welsh rider could have opted to defend the under-23 title she won last year.

But instead she stepped up to elite level and finished 40.11 seconds behind defending champion Marlen Reusser of Switzerland, who retained her crown on her 35th birthday with a winning time of 50 minutes 24.44 seconds.
Backstedt, who started third from last, set the time to beat as she came home 5.43 secs quicker than Germany's Franziska Koch, who eventually finished third.
She told reporters that she started to dream of winning after making a storming start: "In the first half, when I heard the first time check, I was thinking 'OK, maybe it's possible'.

highlights.title: Does AI need an antitrust exemption so it doesn’t kill everyone????
highlights.summary: Today on Decoder, we’ve got the first of a two-part series on the future of business, and I’m talking with Jonathan Kanter, the former antitrust chief for the US Department of Justice in the Biden administration.
body: The biggest story in tech right now is the spiraling debate about AI safety and regulation. Researchers at the big AI labs including Anthropic and Google DeepMind have quit in noisy ways, saying the models pose real threats and safety isn’t being taken seriously across the industry. Other researchers have said the chance of AI killing us all is greater than 10 percent, and the CEOs of all these companies have issued various calls to slow down development and develop regulation, including asking for antitrust exemptions so they can all coordinate on safety issues.

That is a lot of ideas, and I am especially curious about the antitrust piece, which has led to accusations that these companies are seeking regulatory capture, attempting to form a cartel, and even somehow finding a way out from investor pressure ahead of their IPOs.

Jonathan brought huge antitrust cases against Google, Apple, and Ticketmaster during his time as antitrust chief, and along with Lina Khan, led what amounted to a full reboot of American antitrust policy. As you’ll hear him say, he won those cases against Google and Ticketmaster, and that case against Apple is still live in the Trump DOJ, surprising many.

highlights.title: Zach Cregger Finally Made a Perfect Horror-Comedy With 'Resident Evil.' Here's How.
highlights.summary: Comedy typically isn’t my forte; it was one of my primary issues with Weapons. Cregger’s previous film seemed to rely far too much on its comedic elements, often overriding the on-screen tension.
body: Zach Cregger occupies a very strange space in horror filmmaking. Unlike Curry Barker’s Obsession or Kane Parsons’ Backrooms, Resident Evil walks a fine line between comedy and horror, featuring the same dark hilarity as Cregger’s previous films. It’s a tightrope he balances effortlessly, never undermining the tension of certain scary scenes but amplifying them in fascinating ways. You’re almost willing to let your guard down — right up until Cregger hits you with that heart-attack-inducing jump scare.
Resident Evil, by comparison, feels much more confident. It is first and foremost a horror movie filled with moments of blood-curdling terror. The jokes are just there to soften you up.

One of the best examples is the film’s early dog sequence that occurs roughly 20 minutes in. Set on a snow-covered ranch near an abandoned house, the scene begins with the protagonist Bryan (Austin Abrams) being chased by a big, black guard dog in the wake of a car accident. Eventually scrambling into a barn unscathed, he races up a ladder and reaches the safety of the upper level, hitting the dog with a well-timed “Learn to climb, bitch!” as it scrambles to reach him at the foot of the ladder.
points: Comedy typically isn’t my forte; it was one of my primary issues with Weapons.
Cregger’s previous film seemed to rely far too much on its comedic elements, often overriding the on-screen tension.

highlights.title: Hollywood’s Big Night Out: Inside the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art’s Star-Studded Grand Reveal
highlights.summary: On Saturday night, ahead of its September 22 opening, the museum drew a star-studded crowd of Hollywood’s biggest names, from Harrison Ford and Steven Spielberg to Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah Winfrey, Michael B. Jordan, Katy Perry, and Kim Kardashian.
body: Founded by filmmaker George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, the museum is not simply a monument to Star Wars, but a sweeping love letter to the art of storytelling, bringing together paintings, illustrations, photography, animation and cinematic imagery that explore how pictures have the power to shape the stories we tell.

Located in downtown Los Angeles, across from Lucas’s alma mater, the University of Southern California, the museum is a five-story, 300,000-square-foot building featuring 35 galleries and more than 40,000 works. The collection spans celebrated artists including Norman Rockwell, Frida Kahlo, and Banksy, as well as comic art by Jack Kirby. And yes, there are plenty of Star Wars artifacts. The museum’s inaugural exhibition, Star Wars in Motion, showcases vehicles, costumes—including Princess Leia’s—props, and artwork from the first six films. There’s also Luke Skywalker’s Landspeeder and the first physical build of General Grievous’s Wheel Bike from Revenge of the Sith.

highlights.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
highlights.summary: Before two of its alleged members were arrested and charged in Australia last month, the hacker group known as TeamPCP carried out a hacking spree unlike any other in history.
body: Now Google’s threat intelligence group has revealed that during a key moment of TeamPCP’s rampage, the company’s own undercover researcher had infiltrated the group—allowing Google to monitor the hacking spree from the inside, warn breach targets, and even help disrupt the group’s attempts to exploit those victims.

“One of our personas had been working for many months to build trust with one of the actors that was invited to join TeamPCP, and so was added to the group,” Larsen told WIRED in an interview ahead of his LABScon talk. “So essentially, almost day one, Mandiant was watching everything behind the scenes.”

Larsen now says that in March, just as TeamPCP was beginning its frenzied supply-chain hacking, Google’s own undercover analyst was invited to join the hackers’ inner circle. That inside source, whose name Larsen declined to reveal, was one of about 12 members of the group given access to a core chat that TeamPCP called CanisterWorm.
“You guys should understand that we pulled off the biggest supplychain [sic] maybe ever recorded in modern history,” one TeamPCP member wrote in the leaked chats.

highlights.title: Forget the AI Slowdown—the Vulnerability Explosion Is Already Happening
highlights.summary: AI labs are toying with an industry-wide pact to slow development. Meanwhile, widely available AI chatbots are already helping uncover a tidal wave of security flaws.
body: AI doomers have recently traded one worst-case scenario for another, putting aside a potential software vulnerability apocalypse to focus on the possibility of rogue AI causing mass human death in the next decade. As AI leaders consider a cooperative slowdown on frontier model development, though, one aspect of the cybersecurity sea change has already arrived thanks to existing, broadly available capabilities in mainstream AI products, including open weight models.

A tidal wave of vulnerabilities uncovered using AI has only accelerated in recent months—piling more pressure on under-resourced, and very human, IT and security teams and straining volunteers who maintain crucial open source software. Researchers found and disclosed a vast array of vulnerabilities before the rise of AI-enhanced bug hunting as well, but the recent surge is clear.

The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”

Of the victory against Sunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.

“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

highlights.title: Call of Duty maker Activision claims video game cheating is now a £6.3 billion ($8.5 billion) a year industry
highlights.summary: Activision has published a breakdown of the numbers behind cheating in its games, claiming cheating is big business, generating about £6.3 billion - $8.5bn - every year in account sales, boosting, and spoofing services.
body: In a blog posted on the publisher's website, the publisher's cheat squad, Team Ricochet, said cheat subscriptions across 15 games alone generate around £2.6 billion ($3.5 billion).

Activision said it has "paired technical detection with sustained legal action to destabilise the cheat ecosystem at every level", disrupting more than 375 reseller operations, issuing more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and shutting down 31 primary cheat vendors.

The publisher also claims cheat sellers regularly hide the fact their products have been detected, instead blaming outages on excuses like illness, surgery or car accidents to keep customers on side before admitting their cheats are no longer working.

Activision says the crackdown is also driving up costs for cheaters themselves, with subscriptions costing upwards of £75 ($100), spoofing tools adding further recurring fees, and some players spending more than £750 ($1,000) a year in total.

videos.summary: GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards. AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them.
body: The best way to support our work is through our store:
points: GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards.
AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them.
November of 2025 seems like it was the best time to buy, with prices now climbing even past what we saw in February of 2026.
This continues to get worse with thanks to the ongoing DRAM availability crisis thanks to AI data center buildout -- one largely caused by the very companies that make the consumer GPUs.
